solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Like sword in stone, it's 10!
Complex man's complex iPod use?

indicators.note: complex means intricate and tangled, so the letters that follow are knotted into a new order

parts.note: the letters as written

explanation.surface: A jokey psychological diagnosis: someone's tangled relationship with their music player.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'complex' is the anagram signal; the first, capitalised, points to Freud's Oedipus complex.
explanation.definitionFit: Freud named his theory of a son's rivalry with the father after the Greek king, so he is the man behind the complex.

clue.text: Word list fool's written up in delight

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other word that follows

parts.note: to glory in something is to delight in it

indicators.note: in a down clue, writing something upwards means reading it from bottom to top, back to front

parts.note: an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A list of words in which a foolish person has been joyfully written about.
explanation.definitionFit: A glossary is an alphabetical list of terms with their meanings, usually at the back of a book.

clue.text: Reckless Marcus at United denied cross

indicators.note: being denied something means going without it, so that part is taken away

parts.note: Marcus Rashford, the England footballer who came through Manchester United
to ford a river is to cross it

explanation.surface: A footballer's reckless play sees him left out of the side's crosses.
explanation.walkthrough: United here is Manchester United, the English football club where Marcus Rashford made his name.
explanation.definitionFit: Rash describes acting hastily without thought for consequences, which is being reckless.

clue.text: Comedian with Georgia appearing twice in 15 city

parts.note: a wag is a joker or wit
GA is the US postal abbreviation for Georgia
the pair just built is repeated, so it shows up a second time

explanation.surface: A comedian on a double tour with someone called Georgia in an Australian city.
explanation.walkthrough: The pair of pieces is built once and then repeated, as 'appearing twice' says; 15 across is AUSTRALIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Wagga Wagga is a large inland city in New South Wales, Australia.

clue.text: Men worried speak at length

parts.note: OR, other ranks, is military shorthand for soldiers who are not officers
something that ate at you worried you

explanation.surface: Anxious men talk on and on.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to deliver a long formal speech, often pompously.

clue.text: Sea god heading for exit in musical interval

parts.note: Triton, son of Poseidon, the merman god of the sea

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of the next word is used

parts.note: the opening letter of exit

explanation.surface: A sea god leaves to the sound of a musical phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A tritone is an interval spanning three whole tones, the augmented fourth, once called the devil in music.

clue.text: Regular shape needed in theory

parts.note: standard means normal or regular
to model clay is to shape it

explanation.surface: A geometry teacher insists a regular shape is required by the theory.
explanation.definitionFit: The Standard Model is the physics theory describing the fundamental particles and the forces between them.

clue.text: Why Dido let one out is confirmed

indicators.note: out can mean disordered or wrong, so the letters before it are put into another arrangement

parts.note: the letters as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks why Dido released one of something, and is told the fact is confirmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One out' looks like the letter I being removed, but all the words before 'out' are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyed-in-the-wool describes a fixed, thoroughgoing believer, as in a confirmed bachelor or a staunch supporter.

clue.text: One brought in used to ground that's flat

indicators.note: something brought in is taken inside, so this piece goes within the other
ground means crushed and broken up, so the letters are reduced and remixed

parts.note: the letters as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone brought in to work on the land finds it dead level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' reads as land in the surface but is the past tense of grind, signalling the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat in the sense of dull and lifeless is a synonym for tedious, as in a flat performance.

clue.text: Italian covered in sauce shows natural attraction

indicators.note: something covered in a coating sits inside it, so one piece is wrapped by the other

parts.note: gravy is a meat sauce
IT is the standard abbreviation for Italian

explanation.surface: An Italian smothered in sauce shows a fondness for food.
explanation.definitionFit: Gravity is the force by which masses pull towards one another, an attraction built into nature.

clue.text: Scruffs from Campanian city wanting lire

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so a letter is missing from the city

parts.note: Naples is the capital of the Campania region of Italy
L is the abbreviation for the lira, Italy's former currency

explanation.surface: Scruffy people from an Italian city, short of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scruffs' looks like untidy people, but it is the noun for the back of the neck, as in grabbing someone by the scruff.
explanation.definitionFit: The scruff of the neck is its nape, so scruffs are napes.

clue.text: Punish rotter — toxic 15 creature

parts.note: to cane is to punish by beating with a stick
a toad is a contemptible person

explanation.surface: A call to punish some scoundrel who turns out to be a poisonous Australian animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The cane toad was introduced to Australia and is notorious there for its poisonous skin glands.

clue.text: Where traders are quick to hide a blemish

indicators.note: to hide something is to put it out of sight within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: fleet means swift
a, plus a mark, a blemish

explanation.surface: Dealers are quick to conceal a flaw in their goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A flea market is an open-air market where stallholders sell second-hand goods, so it is a place full of traders.

clue.text: Tips on apparel found in one national or another

definitions.note: another national, in contrast to the one already named

indicators.note: found in means located inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a citizen of Austria

indicators.note: the tips of a word are its two ends, so only its outside letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of apparel

explanation.surface: Fashion advice found in one country or another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One national or another' sets two nationalities against each other: the first is the container, the second the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An Australian is a national of Australia, a different nationality from the Austrian in the wordplay.

clue.text: Dracula to open this French wine that's spiked?

indicators.note: a spiked drink has something slipped into it, so a piece is put inside the wine

parts.note: vin is French for wine
a spiked drink is laced with a drug, and E, ecstasy, is the usual one in crosswords

explanation.surface: Dracula is invited to open a bottle of French wine that turns out to be drugged.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes what a vampire's fangs pierce; 'spiked' does double work, signalling the drug and its insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Dracula drinks blood by biting into a blood vessel in the neck, so this is what he opens.

clue.text: Trim line shown with everyone aboard or alongside

indicators.note: aboard means on board, carried inside a vessel, so this piece goes within another

parts.note: to pare is to trim
all means everyone
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A tidy line of people with everyone on board, or else beside the ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Parallel lines run side by side, so to be parallel to something is to be alongside it.

clue.text: Trick allowing last duke to escape old magistrate

indicators.note: allowing the final one to escape means the later of the two matching letters is let go
something that escapes gets away, so this letter leaves the word

parts.note: a dodge is a trick or ruse
D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: A ruse that lets a doomed duke get away from an elderly judge.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick word holds two Ds; 'last' says to remove the second one, not the first.
explanation.definitionFit: The doge was the elected chief magistrate of the old republics of Venice and Genoa.

clue.text: Stomach-related wind mostly an illusion

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: gas is wind, as in flatulence
a trick of the light is an illusion

explanation.surface: A doctor says the digestive wind is largely imaginary.
explanation.definitionFit: Gastric is the medical adjective for anything to do with the stomach.

clue.text: Commercial breaks charm quiet Asian land

indicators.note: to break into something is to get inside it, so this piece interrupts the next word

parts.note: a charm bracelet; a bangle is a rigid bracelet, a piece of jewellery like a charm
an ad is a commercial
sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: TV adverts interrupt a soothing broadcast about an Asian country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charm' looks like an appeal or allure, but here it is an item of jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: Bangladesh is a country in South Asia, bordered mostly by India.

clue.text: Charlemagne in the end destroyed Angers? Angers!

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that letter is taken

parts.note: the final letter of Charlemagne

indicators.note: destroyed means wrecked and broken apart, so the letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: the French city's name, letters as written

explanation.surface: Did the emperor Charlemagne destroy the French city of Angers? The very idea infuriates.
explanation.walkthrough: The first Angers is the city in the Loire valley; the second is the verb meaning provokes.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrage someone is to make them furious, which is to anger them.

clue.text: Old boy joining Vicious and Dury in this rock?

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
Sid Vicious, bassist of the Sex Pistols
Ian Dury, singer of the Blockheads

explanation.surface: An old boy joins two punk stars; is this rock music?
explanation.walkthrough: Sid Vicious and Ian Dury were British punk-era musicians, so 'rock' looks like music but is stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Obsidian is a glassy black volcanic rock formed when lava cools very quickly.

clue.text: Reversed second line in Daily Record

indicators.note: reversed means turned back to front, so the next word is read backwards

parts.note: to second someone is to aid them
RY, railway, is a line

explanation.surface: A second line of text appears back to front in a Scottish newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Daily Record is a Scottish tabloid, but here the words simply mean a record kept every day.
explanation.definitionFit: A diary is a book in which one records events day by day.

clue.text: Archer's first and last quarrel?

definitions.note: the question mark flags the crossbow sense rather than an argument

indicators.note: first and last pick the two ends of the preceding word, discarding its middle

parts.note: the opening and closing letters of archer
a row is a quarrel

explanation.surface: An archer's first and final argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarrel' does double duty: an argument for the wordplay and a crossbow bolt for the definition, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarrel is a square-headed bolt shot from a crossbow, a kind of arrow.

clue.text: Larks circling a goat-legged deity

indicators.note: circling means going round, so one piece surrounds the next

parts.note: larks are fun, high jinks
taken as written

explanation.surface: Birds wheel around a half-goat god.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Larks' looks like the birds, but means jokes and games.
explanation.definitionFit: A faun is a Roman rural god with a man's upper body and the legs and horns of a goat.

clue.text: Flag shown with damage carried in E-boat?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something carried in a vessel travels inside it, so this piece goes within the boat

parts.note: Noah's ark is the crossword's favourite boat
to mar is to damage

explanation.surface: A wartime German torpedo boat flying a damaged flag.
explanation.walkthrough: An E-boat was a German fast attack craft of the Second World War; here it splits into E and a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: To flag something is to mark it for attention, and to earmark is to set aside or tag for a purpose.

clue.text: Declare shortly: runs at Oval scored briskly

indicators.note: shortly means in a cut-down form, so the word is clipped at its end

parts.note: to allege is to declare or assert
R is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for runs
an O is oval in shape

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator: runs were scored quickly at the Oval, so declare soon.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oval is a London cricket ground, and declaring is when a captain ends an innings; here 'scored' means written in music.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegro is the tempo marking in a musical score telling players to perform at a lively, brisk pace.

clue.text: GCHQ sort can party insanely (then said to keel over)

indicators.note: insanely means madly, so these letters are jumbled crazily

parts.note: the letters as written

indicators.note: said tells us to take the sound of the word rather than its spelling

parts.note: a ship that lists leans over to one side

explanation.surface: The staff of Britain's spy agency party wildly and then collapse drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: GCHQ is Britain's signals intelligence headquarters, famous for code-breaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptanalyst breaks codes and ciphers, the core work of an agency like GCHQ.
